We administer NCEA and ensure New Zealand qualifications are accepted as credible and robust. | The New Zealand Qualifications Authority - Mana Tohu Mātauranga o Aotearoa (NZQA) is responsible for ensuring that New Zealand qualifications are accepted as credible and robust, nationally and internationally. 

Our work with qualifications and micro-credentials helps people show potential employers what they know, and what they can do.

Our role includes:
- managing the New Zealand Qualifications Framework
- administering the NCEA secondary school assessment system
- conducting independent quality assurance of non-university tertiary education providers
- undertaking qualifications recognition and standard-setting for some specified unit standards.">

          <p class="break-words text-color-text" data-test-id="about-us__description">
              The New Zealand Qualifications Authority - Mana Tohu Mātauranga o Aotearoa (NZQA) is responsible for ensuring that New Zealand qualifications are accepted as credible and robust, nationally and internationally. 

Our work with qualifications and micro-credentials helps people show potential employers what they know, and what they can do.

Our role includes:
- managing the New Zealand Qualifications Framework
- administering the NCEA secondary school assessment system
- conducting independent quality assurance of non-university tertiary education providers
- undertaking qualifications recognition and standard-setting for some specified unit standards.

We also help people to have certain types of qualifications recognised internationally.  This means people with New Zealand diplomas, degrees and other qualifications can work overseas, and skilled people from other countries can have their qualifications recognised in New Zealand.

NZQA's vision is to help people "Qualify for the Future World: Kia noho takatū ki tō āmua ao", with two focus areas:
- Equity of access to qualifications supports intergenerational wellbeing
- New Zealand qualifications enable lifelong learning

For information about how we use LinkedIn, please see the Social Media Terms of Use on our website.

Dame Susan brings extensive experience in educational leadership and governance. She is Chancellor of the University of Waikato, having previously served as Pro-Chancellor (2018 to 2025) and as a member of the University Council since 2016. She was Headmaster of Hamilton Boys High School from 1999 to 2024 and is also a member of the Teaching Council’s Governing Council.

Ravi brings international experience in leading organisations through complex technology and digital change. He helps boards make clear, risk-aware decisions on technology investment, AI, cyber and data resilience.

Additional Board changes include the reappointment of Professor Wiremu Doherty and Jeremy Baker, and the resignation of David Ferguson.</p>

Whakatairangatia ngā kete o te mātauranga ki te ao mārama! E te tai whakarunga, e te tai whakararo, nau piki mai, nau kake mai ki te Mana Tohu Mātauranga o Aotearoa. May the baskets of knowledge be brought into the world of light. We welcome one and all to join us at the New Zealand Qualifications Authority.

NZQA is looking for our next Pou Whakahaere Tuarua Māori - Deputy Chief Executive Māori to lead the Office of the DCE Māori.

It’s a small team that provides strategic direction, thought leadership and specialist advice to help ensure NZQA is positioned to meet the future needs of the education sector, particularly in relation to ākonga Māori achievement, Māori learner success and the protection and promotion of mātauranga Māori across qualifications, quality assurance and assessment. 
 
The DCE Māori provides te ao Māori leadership across NZQA, champions Māori standards and qualifications and works in partnership with leaders across the organisation to embed Māori perspectives, strengthen organisational capability and support a coherent Māori leadership eco-system. 
 
The role leads NZQA’s engagement with Ngā Kaitūhono, iwi and external Māori stakeholders, and works across the public sector and education system to influence outcomes for Māori learners and uphold strong Māori–Crown relationships.
 
If this interests you, follow the link to find out more: <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/eN4YGaca?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/eN4YGaca</a> </p>

     assessments
